clue.text: Carol and Lily mended in confusion, which is how we clued the other Across clues

definitions.text: which is how we clued the other Across clues

parts.note: to carol is to sing, as carollers do

indicators.note: the words Lily mended are thrown into confusion, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women named Carol and Lily patch something up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the puzzle's gimmick: every other Across answer is clued as if each doubled letter were single, so it enters the grid with a letter more than its wordplay gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as single-minded-ly, the phrase says the clues were written with doubled letters thought of as single ones.

clue.text: One taking major steps gutted significant additional clause

indicators.note: with its insides removed only the first and last letters of significant remain

parts.note: taken as written
a rider is a clause added to a bill or contract

explanation.surface: A significant extra clause in a contract has been stripped of its substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A strider walks with long, purposeful paces, the big steps of the definition.

clue.text: The greatest group of nine almost adopting earth tone

indicators.note: the shortened group takes the earth colour into itself
the group's word loses its last letter, so it is not quite complete

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A nine-piece band nearly takes on a brown, earthy sound and becomes the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the top position, the best of all, like the hit at the top of a chart.

clue.text: Relaxed call?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: the word laid put back to front gives dial, to call on the phone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is an instruction: laid, back, spells dial, and to dial is to call.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back describes someone easygoing and calm, and taken as a direction it turns laid into a telephone verb.

clue.text: Mounting a precious stone that's huge

indicators.note: in a down answer mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Setting a jewel in a mount, and it's an enormous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for enormous or tremendous, a near synonym of huge.

clue.text: City in the South: Salerno?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Louisiana city on the Mississippi
second meaning, read cryptically: the Italian city's name is the word Orleans given a new arrangement

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a reverse anagram: rearranging Orleans gives Salerno, so Salerno is a new Orleans.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the largest city in Louisiana in the American South, famous for jazz.

clue.text: Lombardi, after end of game show

indicators.note: the coach's first name is placed after that letter
only the closing letter of game is used

parts.note: taken as written; its last letter is used
Vince Lombardi was the famous Green Bay Packers football coach

explanation.surface: Coach Lombardi appears on a TV show after the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality, as in evincing surprise.

clue.text: Free time put into building toy

indicators.note: the time abbreviation goes inside the toy's name

parts.note: Lego is the plastic brick construction toy

explanation.surface: A child is given free time to play with building blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to release, to set something free.

clue.text: Kind of angel I mistreated

indicators.note: the letters are handled roughly and so knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they mistreated a sort of angel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind looks like 'sort', as in kind of angel, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and good-natured, so kind as an adjective fits.

clue.text: Circle around in the morning, crashing into…

indicators.note: the word for circle goes around the morning abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a ring is a circle
AM, ante meridiem, marks a morning time

explanation.surface: Something goes round and round in the morning before crashing into whatever comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: As the preamble-style 1 Across explains, the wordplay gives the word with one M; the grid doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramming is driving forcefully against something, which is what a vehicle crashing into another does.

clue.text: …line in colorless trim

indicators.note: the line's abbreviation is placed in the word for colorless

parts.note: white is often treated as the absence of colour

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, something crashes into a pale strip of trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single T; the grid doubles it, as 1 Across says.
explanation.definitionFit: To whittle is to pare or cut down a little at a time, a synonym of trim as a verb.

clue.text: Down with networks and nerds

parts.note: a web is a network, of threads or of links

explanation.surface: Down with the online crowd and the nerds, says a disgruntled protester.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single E; the grid doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a socially awkward, studious person, the same as a nerd.

clue.text: Sib replacing bacterium's energy in vegetable

indicators.note: the sibling word takes the place of the energy symbol inside the bacterium's name

parts.note: E. coli is the familiar gut bacterium
a bro is a brother, a sibling

explanation.surface: A lab scenario in which a relative's germs have spread into the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single C; the grid doubles it. E is the physics symbol for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green plant of the cabbage family eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: A collection of stars or athletes from Detroit, shifting 50 into a wager

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the 50 letter is moved out of the team name

parts.note: the Detroit Lions are an NFL football team

indicators.note: the moved letter goes inside the wager word

parts.note: a bet is a wager
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A sports writer weighs a constellation against Detroit athletes betting fifty dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: One piece does two jobs: the L shifted out of the team name is the L that goes into the wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion's Belt is the row of three bright stars across the middle of the Orion constellation, an asterism.

clue.text: Retro poet's contraction, made better, arose again

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: o'er is the poetic shortening of over
cured means healed, made better

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned poet's shortened word, once improved, has come back into use.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single C and a single R; the grid doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: To reoccur is to happen again, so something that reoccurred came up a second time.

clue.text: Dog returning what I threw?

indicators.note: the dog's word is turned to run the other way

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A dog comes back with the thing its owner threw for it to fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives one L; the grid doubles it. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is the classic object an owner throws for a dog to fetch and bring back.

clue.text: Fishing bait is lame, wrong, messed-up

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are messed up into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that some fishing bait is feeble, wrong and badly mangled.
explanation.definitionFit: An angleworm is an earthworm used as bait by anglers on a hook.

clue.text: Baseball Hall of Famer traveled west, taking an automobile

indicators.note: the travel word takes the vehicle into itself

parts.note: rode means traveled on a horse or vehicle
a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: A baseball great went west by car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Carew, a seven-time batting champion with the Twins and Angels, was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1991.

clue.text: Nourish government agent

wordplay.note: a fed is an American federal agent, such as an FBI officer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a double definition, but the agent is the three-letter word; the grid doubles its E to give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed someone is to give them food, which is to nourish them.

clue.text: Search for maturity

parts.note: taken as written
age can mean being grown up, as in coming of age

explanation.surface: Looking for maturity in someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Search for reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Search and for is a piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to hunt around for food or supplies, a kind of searching.

clue.text: Spy on (stare at) wasteful endeavor

parts.note: James Bond is fiction's best-known spy
to ogle is to stare at lecherously

explanation.surface: Keeping watch on someone and staring at them turns out to be a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single O and a single G; the grid doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: A boondoggle is American slang for a pointless, money-wasting project, often publicly funded.

clue.text: Photography pioneer adjusted a steam nozzle's opening

indicators.note: the letters are adjusted, set into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers with a steam nozzle's outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening looks like the nozzle's mouth; here it takes only the first letter of nozzle's.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eastman founded Kodak and popularised roll film, making photography available to everyone.

clue.text: Zigzag look in pan

indicators.note: the old word for look sits inside the word for pan

parts.note: to pan a show is to slam it, criticise it harshly
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone takes a look in a cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan looks like cookware but is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slalom is to ski or move in a zigzag course around obstacles.

clue.text: Steals cattle with no evidence of neglect

wordplay.note: a rustler is a cattle thief, so he rustles

explanation.surface: A cattle thief leaves no trace of carelessness behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the cattle thief's verb; the grid doubles its S to give the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustless metal has no rust, the corrosion that shows a thing has been left uncared for.

clue.text: Colossal volley contents!

indicators.note: the answer is part of what the two words contain, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: taken as written; the run of letters bridging the two words is used

explanation.surface: An exclamation about what an enormous barrage contains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the hiding instruction and, read as a whole, a description of a salvo.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a volley of fire, and a colossal volley is just that.

clue.text: Reach those with expertise

wordplay.note: aces are experts, people who excel at something

explanation.surface: Experts are within reach, or reach the experts.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single C and a single S; the grid doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: To access something is to get at it or get to it, a verb sense close to reach.

clue.text: We hear second son is competent

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of a word, not its spelling

parts.note: Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve in Genesis

explanation.surface: We're told a family's younger son is capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill or power to do something, the same as capable.

clue.text: Storm engulfs Long Island, where Jesus once walked

indicators.note: the storm word swallows the island's abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, a storm
LI is the standard abbreviation for New York's Long Island

explanation.surface: A storm sweeps over Long Island, with a nod to the place Jesus walked on water.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single E; the grid doubles it. Jesus walked on the Sea of Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: Galilee, a region of northern Israel with its lake, is where the Gospels place Jesus walking on water.

clue.text: Rambo getting drunk in a saloon

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of the hero's name stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The action hero Rambo is getting drunk in a saloon.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives a single R and a single O; the grid doubles both.
explanation.definitionFit: A barroom is a room where drinks are served over a bar, which is what a saloon is.

clue.text: Farm animal swallowing bug — a sign for some female politicians

indicators.note: the farm animal takes the bug inside it

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
a mite is a tiny bug
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A cow eating an insect is taken as a portent by women in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a single M, T and E; the grid doubles all three.
explanation.definitionFit: Committeewomen are women who sit on a party committee, typically representing a district in American politics.
